chapter: New Orleans clarinetists and Steve Lewis
title: Steve Lewis the pianist and singer
summary: Steve Lewis, piano player and singer of smutty songs, drawing crowds and money and drinking, and Handy's remark on Piron's difficult music.

blocks.x: What kind of guy was Steve Lewis? Steve Lewis? Mm-hmm.
Oh, Steve Lewis is a wonderful piano player. Likes to crack a lot of jokes, and he sing a lot of songs with a lot of smutty things to it.
I don't know. Did you ever know Papa D. Dot Dot? No, I don't think. You ever know Papa D. Dot Dot? No, I don't think. You ever know Papa D. Dot Dot? No, I don't think.
You ever know Papa D. Dot Dot? No, I don't think.

I don't think I know. He was one of Steve's buddies. He was always getting in trouble, you know, and Steve would get him out of jail. Oh, yeah? No, I don't know him. Uh, what would these songs be about that Steve Lewis would sing?

Anything come in his mind. Yeah, anything come in his mind, he'd say it. Yeah, he didn't care what he said, the way he said it, anything come in his mind, he'd say stuff I know he was playing there on the Island Charter. Man you couldn't get in the place. From the time he get there and the time he leave. He get there around. He do that eight. He get there around ten, eleven. Anytime. But the people still be there waiting for him when he come in. Man he walk back there and the people give him a big glass of whiskey with the served beer. That's what they give him whiskey. He take him a big drink of there and sit on the piano. Man he started singing back there. And there's no way in the world for you to get back there to him. All the people around him. Just giving him money. Making him sing. Giving him money. Making him sing. And get him drunk. And then they used to take him from there. He used to leave there around three or four o'clock in the morning. They take him from there. They take him to the Roosevelt Hotel. Somewhere up in there. And have him sing up there until nine, ten o'clock the next day. He made a lot of money. Then he was a, you know, thing. Then he was a, he was a regular guy. Fine, fine guy, Steve was. That's the only fault P. Roy had of him drinking so much. Never messed up. He'd go ahead and play but he just, he likes to drink. And then P. Roy didn't like that. Did you work much with P. Roy? No. No, I didn't do much playing with P. Roy because P. Roy had a lot of hard music and I couldn't cut it. That's good. He wouldn't run an affair with your playing or something. Yeah, well I didn't, uh, he kept a lot of stock. I don't even. He kept a lot of arrangements for his band. And, uh, I used to do a lot of rehearsals. And, uh, for you to just go sit in there, you had to be pretty good. Excuse me, go ahead. Unless he was playing Dinah or High Society or something like that.
